prompt: Write the body (about 150 words) of an insurer's answer to a personal injury petition in Texas: a general denial and three affirmative defenses that fit a parking lot collision. Plain text. Call the parties only 'Plaintiff' and 'Defendant'. No names, placeholders, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1282; do not mention it.)
text:
Defendant, appearing subject to and without waiving its right to a jury trial, files this Original Answer to Plaintiff's Original Petition and respectfully shows the Court as follows.

General Denial. Pursuant to Texas Rule of Civil Procedure 92, Defendant generally denies each and every allegation contained in Plaintiff's Original Petition and demands strict proof thereof by a preponderance of the evidence, as required by the Constitution and laws of the State of Texas.

First Affirmative Defense: Proportionate Responsibility. Defendant asserts that any injury or damage Plaintiff sustained was caused in whole or in part by Plaintiff's own negligence, including failure to keep a proper lookout and failure to yield in the parking area. Under Chapter 33 of the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code, any recovery must be reduced by Plaintiff's percentage of responsibility, and Defendant is not liable if that percentage exceeds fifty percent.

Second Affirmative Defense: Sole Proximate Cause. The conduct of a third party over whom Defendant had no control was the sole proximate cause of the occurrence described in the Petition.

Third Affirmative Defense: Failure to Mitigate. Plaintiff failed to exercise reasonable care to mitigate damages, and any recovery must be reduced accordingly.
